sentences.en: Nelson gazed out at the spires of the Danish capital.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊凝视着丹麦首都的尖塔。

sentences.en: With luck he thought, the enemy would soon come to terMs.
sentences.zh: 他心想，运气好的话，敌人很快就会妥协。

sentences.en: And he could leave the city unscathed.
sentences.zh: 这样他就能安然无恙地离开这座城市。

sentences.en: That night, he invited his captains aboard the elephant for a final dinner.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，他邀请各位舰长登上“象号”战舰共进最后的晚餐。

sentences.en: He was in the highest spirits, one remembered, and drank to the success of the ensuing day.
sentences.zh: 据回忆，他当时兴致极高，还为次日的胜利举杯祝酒。

sentences.en: As they left, Nelson shook each man by the hand and wished him luck.
sentences.zh: 临走时，纳尔逊与每一个人握手，并祝他们好运。

sentences.en: When they had gone, he lay sleepless in his cot, listening to the creak of the timbers.
sentences.zh: 他们走后，他躺在行军床上辗转反侧，听着木材的吱呀声。

sentences.en: Everything, he thought, depended on a fair wind to push them into the enemy's harbour.
sentences.zh: 他心想，一切都取决于能否有一阵顺风将他们推入敌人的港口。

sentences.en: Dawn came.
sentences.zh: 黎明降临。

sentences.en: Thursday, the 2nd of April, 1801.
sentences.zh: 1801 年 4 月 2 日，星期四。

sentences.en: Another grey, dreary day.
sentences.zh: 又是阴沉沉的一天。

sentences.en: But as Nelson stepped onto the quarterdeck, a smile spread across his face.
sentences.zh: 但当纳尔逊踏上后甲板时，脸上露出了笑容。

sentences.en: The wind had changed.
sentences.zh: 风向变了。

sentences.en: And was blowing from the southeaSt.
sentences.zh: 正从东南方吹来。

sentences.en: The conditions could not have been better.
sentences.zh: 条件再好不过了。

sentences.en: His personal troubles were forgotten.
sentences.zh: 他个人的烦恼已被抛诸脑后。

sentences.en: This was his world.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的世界。

sentences.en: The swell of the sea.
sentences.zh: 海浪的起伏。

sentences.en: The burden of command.
sentences.zh: 指挥的重担。

sentences.en: The thrill of battle.
sentences.zh: 战斗的快感。

sentences.en: God was with them, he thought.
sentences.zh: 他心想，上帝与他们同在。

sentences.en: And ordered his crew to hoist signal 14.
sentences.zh: 于是下令船员升起 14 号信号旗。

sentences.en: Prepare for battle.
sentences.zh: 准备战斗。

sentences.en: A thrilling and thoroughly patriotic scene from What Else?
sentences.zh: 这是来自《还有什么？》中一段激动人心且极具爱国情怀的场景。

sentences.en: Adventures in Time, Nelson, Hero of the Seas, by top Nelson scholar Dominic Sandbrook.
sentences.zh: 由顶级纳尔逊研究学者多米尼克·桑德布鲁克所著的《时间冒险：海上英雄纳尔逊》。

sentences.en: Out last week, I think, in paperback.
sentences.zh: 我想上周刚出了平装本。

sentences.en: So, a splendid read.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一本精彩的读物。

sentences.en: And, I mean, the drama of it.
sentences.zh: 而且，我是说，这其中的戏剧性。

sentences.en: We're in the spring of 1801, and Britain is facing a potentially mortal threat to her very survival as an independent power.
sentences.zh: 时间是 1801 年春天，英国正面临着作为独立大国生存下去的致命威胁。

sentences.en: So, there is a huge strategic crisis that has hoved into view.
sentences.zh: 所以，一场巨大的战略危机已经显现。

sentences.en: Britain, if she is to have any hope of maintaining her independence against France, needs to control the seas.
sentences.zh: 英国若想保住对抗法国的独立地位，就必须控制海洋。

sentences.en: But the problem is that a new Tsar, Paul I, hates a waistcoat, loves issuing intemperate orders to his servants.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，新沙皇保罗一世讨厌背心，却喜欢对仆人下达不理智的命令。

sentences.en: He has organised a new league of armed neutrality, which actually isn't neutral at all, because
sentences.zh: 他组织了一个新的武装中立联盟，但这实际上根本不中立，因为

sentences.en: it's directly targeted at the monopoly of supplies that Britain needs to maintain the Royal Navy.
sentences.zh: 它直接针对英国维持皇家海军所需的物资垄断。

sentences.en: And this would then facilitate the growth of the French Navy, thereby threatening Britain's command of the seas.
sentences.zh: 这将促进法国海军的发展，从而威胁到英国对海洋的控制权。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, what is Britain to do?
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，英国该怎么办？

sentences.en: When you're faced with a national emergency, who do you send for?
sentences.zh: 当你面临国家紧急状态时，你会派谁去？

sentences.en: Well, they send for Nelson, because, as you've described, the countries of the Baltic have
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们派了纳尔逊，因为正如你所描述的，波罗的海国家

sentences.en: let themselves down by forming this league of armed neutrality, especially, I have to say, the Danes.
sentences.zh: 通过组建这个武装中立联盟让自己陷入了困境，我不得不说，尤其是丹麦人。

sentences.en: I know, who are almost like Englishmen, according to Nelson.
sentences.zh: 我知道，据纳尔逊说，他们几乎就像英国人一样。

sentences.en: And you don't get higher praise than that, do you?
sentences.zh: 你得不到比这更高的评价了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Right, they're a slightly worse version of Englishmen.
sentences.zh: 没错，他们是稍微差一点的英国人。

sentences.en: And for them to rank themselves alongside the Russians, and as you say, implicitly, the
sentences.zh: 让他们与俄国人并列，正如你所说，隐含地与

sentences.en: French, because this will be a gift to Napoleon Bonaparte.
sentences.zh: 法国人并列，因为这对拿破仑·波拿巴来说将是一份大礼。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the real shocker, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这才是真正令人震惊的地方，不是吗？

sentences.en: It is, exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实，正是如此。

sentences.en: So, the Admiralty's reaction has been to send this squadron east, to break this league by force, and first in line is the Danish fleet and the dockyards at Copenhagen.
sentences.zh: 所以，海军部的反应是派遣这支分遣舰队向东，武力瓦解这个联盟，首当其冲的就是丹麦舰队和哥本哈根的造船厂。

sentences.en: And listeners who remember our last episode will recall that the commander of the fleet is not Nelson.
sentences.zh: 记得我们上一集的听众会记得，舰队的指挥官并不是纳尔逊。

sentences.en: It is the elderly Admiral Sir Hyde Parker, who has somehow managed to tear himself away from the delights of his teenage bride.
sentences.zh: 而是年迈的海德·帕克爵士，他好不容易才从他那十几岁新娘的温柔乡中抽身出来。

sentences.en: This is the paradox, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是矛盾所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: That the reason, perhaps, why Nelson hasn't been given command is because there's a slight shadow over his reputation as a consequence of his affair with Emma Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 也许纳尔逊没有被授予指挥权的原因，是因为他与艾玛·汉密尔顿的绯闻给他的名声蒙上了一层阴影。

sentences.en: But Sir Hyde Parker isn't a model of propriety at all.
sentences.zh: 但海德·帕克爵士根本不是什么道德楷模。

sentences.en: It takes all sorts.
sentences.zh: 什么样的人都有。

sentences.en: I don't want to pronounce on the nature of his relationship with this young woman.
sentences.zh: 我不想对他们之间的关系性质妄加评论。

sentences.en: As you rightly say, there is this shadow hanging over Horatio Nelson, which is the fact that he has abandoned his wife, Fanny, for Emma Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，霍雷肖·纳尔逊身上确实笼罩着阴影，那就是他为了艾玛·汉密尔顿抛弃了他的妻子范妮。

sentences.en: And I see that you've added the words, luscious, in the notes, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我看到你在笔记里加了“诱人”这个词，汤姆。

sentences.en: You, in your notes, have described Emma as vile.
sentences.zh: 你在笔记里把艾玛描述为“卑鄙”。

sentences.en: I've crossed that out.
sentences.zh: 我已经把它划掉了。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's an accurate description of her.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为这是对她准确的描述。

sentences.en: Listeners can make up their own minds, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，听众可以自己做判断。

sentences.en: We pride ourselves, don't we, that we have these little disagreements, unlike some goal-hanger podcasts, which boast of disagreeing agreeably, but never disagree about anything.
sentences.zh: 我们引以为豪的是，我们会有这些小分歧，不像某些只会随声附和的播客，吹嘘自己能和谐地持有不同意见，但实际上对任何事情都没有分歧。

sentences.en: That's not the case on the rest of his history.
sentences.zh: 在《历史的其余部分》中可不是这样。

sentences.en: No, we disagree about top mistresses and other such vital topics.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们会为了顶级情妇和其他此类重要话题争论不休。

sentences.en: We do, exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实，正是如此。

sentences.en: So he ended last time with intelligence reaching the fleet, that Copenhagen's defences are even more formidable than Parker and Nelson expected.
sentences.zh: 所以上次我们讲到情报传到舰队，哥本哈根的防御比帕克和纳尔逊预想的还要强大。

sentences.en: Huge citadel batteries, two massive forts bristling with guns.
sentences.zh: 巨大的堡垒炮台，两座布满火炮的庞大要塞。

sentences.en: And the Danes have created this defensive line, this kind of wall of guns made up of warships and hulks and sort of floating gun platforms facing the sea.
sentences.zh: 丹麦人还建立了这条防御线，这种由战舰、废弃船只和浮动炮台组成的火炮之墙，面向大海。

sentences.en: And there's one particular fortress, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 而且还有一个特别的堡垒，不是吗？

sentences.en: There's kind of outside, which is built on solid rock.
sentences.zh: 外面有一个，是建在坚硬岩石上的。

sentences.en: So that's also got to be negotiated.
sentences.zh: 所以这也必须解决掉。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And of course, the water is very shallow.
sentences.zh: 当然，水非常浅。

sentences.en: As always in naval battles, there's lots of action with shoals.
sentences.zh: 和所有海战一样，浅滩有很多动作空间。

sentences.en: So they have to get around this.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须绕过这个。

sentences.en: Flat bottoMs.
sentences.zh: 平底船。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The shoal.
sentences.zh: 浅滩。

sentences.en: So Nelson has urged Admiral Parker to launch the attack anyway.
sentences.zh: 所以纳尔逊敦促帕克海军上将无论如何都要发动进攻。

sentences.en: Never did our country depend so much on the success of any fleet as on this.
sentences.zh: 我国从未像现在这样依赖任何一支舰队的成功。

sentences.en: And we ended with Parker's answer, which is, sure, all right, but you will lead the attack personally.
sentences.zh: 我们上次讲到帕克的回答是，好吧，没问题，但你得亲自领导进攻。

sentences.en: Now, some people would find that daunting.
sentences.zh: 现在，有些人会觉得这很令人生畏。

sentences.en: Of course, Nelson is not a man to be daunted.
sentences.zh: 当然，纳尔逊不是一个会被吓倒的人。

sentences.en: He's excited.
sentences.zh: 他很兴奋。

sentences.en: He's thrilled.
sentences.zh: 他很激动。

sentences.en: On the 27th of March, he moves his flag from the St. George, which is the ship he'd been given back in England, to the 74-gun ship Elephant.
sentences.zh: 3 月 27 日，他将指挥旗从他在英国时被分配的“圣乔治号”移到了 74 门炮的“象号”战舰上。

sentences.en: The Elephant, as Andrew Lambert points out, ironically, the badge of the Danish monarchy.
sentences.zh: 正如安德鲁·兰伯特指出的那样，讽刺的是，“象号”正是丹麦君主制的标志。

sentences.en: And the reason he's moving, isn't it, is that the Elephant has what naval people call a shallower draught.
sentences.zh: 他搬过去的原因，是因为“象号”有海军所说的较浅的吃水，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Talk us through the shallower draught.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲较浅的吃水吧。

sentences.en: Well, it means it's better able to cope with the shallows because, Dominic, it draws less water.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这意味着它更能应对浅水区，因为多米尼克，它的吃水更浅。

sentences.en: Oh, does it?
sentences.zh: 哦，是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: Basically, it can go in shallower water than the St. George can.
sentences.zh: 基本上，它能进入比“圣乔治号”更浅的水域。

sentences.en: So that's why he moves.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他搬过去的原因。

sentences.en: And of course, when he moves, he makes sure to take with him his two most prized possessions, which are portraits of Emma, his guardian angels, he calls them.
sentences.zh: 当然，搬过去的时候，他一定要带上他最珍视的两件物品，那就是艾玛的肖像，他称之为他的守护天使。

sentences.en: So they go into his new cabin.
sentences.zh: 所以它们被带进了他的新船舱。

sentences.en: So that's splendid.
sentences.zh: 那真是太棒了。

sentences.en: That's very moving.
sentences.zh: 那非常感人。

sentences.en: So from the Elephant, he will command this squadron of six other 74s.
sentences.zh: 所以他将从“象号”上指挥这支由其他六艘 74 门炮战舰组成的分遣队。

sentences.en: So the 74-gun ship is the sort of classic warship of the Royal Navy.
sentences.zh: 74 门炮战舰是皇家海军经典的战舰类型。

sentences.en: So you've got the Defiance, the Ganges, the Edgar, the Bellona, the Russell, and the Monarch.
sentences.zh: 你有“蔑视号”、“恒河号”、“埃德加号”、“贝罗纳号”、“罗素号”和“君主号”。

sentences.en: And there are three 64-gun ships.
sentences.zh: 还有三艘 64 门炮战舰。

sentences.en: And there are various frigates and fire ships.
sentences.zh: 以及各种护卫舰和火船。

sentences.en: And crucially, there are seven bomb vessels.
sentences.zh: 最关键的是，有七艘轰炸舰。

sentences.en: And these are ships that will start shelling the Danish dockyards once Nelson's warships have cleared out the defences.
sentences.zh: 这些船将在纳尔逊的战舰清除防御后，开始炮击丹麦的造船厂。

sentences.en: And Dominic, just a couple of things to say about that.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，关于这一点有几件事要说。

sentences.en: Firstly, the Edgar, one of the ships, named after Athelstan's nephew.
sentences.zh: 首先，“埃德加号”，其中一艘船，是以埃塞尔斯坦的侄子命名的。

sentences.en: And Athelstan, of course, defeated the Danes.
sentences.zh: 当然，埃塞尔斯坦击败了丹麦人。

sentences.en: So maybe there's a slight kind of portent there.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这有一点预兆。

sentences.en: And the other thing is the identity of one of Nelson's captains, who is in command of a 56er.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是纳尔逊的一位舰长的身份，他指挥着一艘 56 门炮的战舰。

sentences.en: So not quite as many guns, but still very, very formidable, as we'll see.
sentences.zh: 虽然炮火没那么多，但正如我们将看到的，依然非常非常强大。

sentences.en: This is a ship called the HMS Glatton.
sentences.zh: 这是一艘名为“格拉顿号”的英国皇家海军战舰。

sentences.en: And the commander of that is Captain Bly, who 12 years before had been in command of a ship called the Bounty in the Pacific Ocean that had witnessed a famous mutiny.
sentences.zh: 指挥官是布莱船长，12 年前他曾在太平洋指挥过一艘名为“邦蒂号”的船，并目睹了一场著名的叛乱。

sentences.en: So Bly has lots to prove.
sentences.zh: 所以布莱有很多东西要证明。

sentences.en: And fortunately, the Glatton is a kind of ship that would enable him to prove things because it's armed with this new kind of cannon, the Caronade, which is very short range.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，“格拉顿号”这种船能让他证明自己，因为它装备了一种新型火炮——卡隆炮，射程非常短。

sentences.en: So if you can get the ship up close, it will inflict incredible damage on its target.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你能让船靠近，它会对目标造成难以置信的破坏。

sentences.en: Massive guns, and they are mounted on pivot so they can swivel round and they sweep at a range of targets.
sentences.zh: 巨大的火炮，安装在枢轴上，可以旋转，横扫一系列目标。

sentences.en: And as we will see, this makes the Glatton a very, very formidable addition to Nelson's armory.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将看到的，这使得“格拉顿号”成为纳尔逊军火库中非常非常强大的补充。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But getting into the harbour is going to be a tough job.
sentences.zh: 但进入港口将是一项艰巨的任务。

sentences.en: They're waiting for the wind to sweep them in.
sentences.zh: 他们正在等待风把他们吹进去。

sentences.en: And they haven't even got up to Copenhagen yet.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至还没到哥本哈根。

sentences.en: So on the 30th of March, the wind finally shifts because they've been waiting for three days.
sentences.zh: 所以 3 月 30 日，风终于转了，因为他们已经等了三天了。

sentences.en: And they sail south into the Öresund, which is the strait between Denmark and Sweden.
sentences.zh: 他们向南航行进入厄勒海峡，那是丹麦和瑞典之间的海峡。

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: It's called the Öresund.
sentences.zh: 它叫厄勒海峡。

sentences.en: Master of tongues.
sentences.zh: 语言大师。

sentences.en: I'm just guessing.
sentences.zh: 我只是猜的。

sentences.en: I saw an O with an accent and I thought I'd mix it up a bit.
sentences.zh: 我看到一个带重音符号的O，就想稍微混搭一下。

sentences.en: Anyway, they sail into this strait and ahead is this great fortress of Kronborg, which is the castle of Elsinore, as in Hamlet.
sentences.zh: 总之，他们驶入了这个海峡，前方就是宏伟的克隆堡要塞，也就是哈姆雷特里的那个埃尔西诺城堡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they're worried that there are great guns at the castle, so they go over to the Swedish side of the strait.
sentences.zh: 他们担心城堡里有重炮，所以就绕到了海峡的瑞典一侧。

sentences.en: Although, Dominic, there's a risk there as well, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 不过，多米尼克，那里也有风险，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because Sweden also is part of this league.
sentences.zh: 因为瑞典也是这个联盟的一部分。

sentences.en: They don't know how many guns might be there and whether the Swedes would fire them.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道那里会有多少大炮，也不知道瑞典人会不会开火。

sentences.en: The Swedes are not cut from the same cloth that they were in the Great Northern War, I think, by this point.
sentences.zh: 我想，到这个时候，瑞典人已经不像大北方战争时期那样硬气了。

sentences.en: They've already started to move in a Greta Thunberg-style direction.
sentences.zh: 他们已经开始向格蕾塔·通贝里那种风格转变了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because they don't fire.
sentences.zh: 因为他们根本没开火。

sentences.en: And actually, it turns out they don't really have any guns there anyway.
sentences.zh: 事实上，结果证明他们那里根本就没什么大炮。

sentences.en: So Nelson's Gamble pays off.
sentences.zh: 所以纳尔逊的赌注赢了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: So the Danish guns can't reach the British ships.
sentences.zh: 所以丹麦的大炮根本够不着英国军舰。

sentences.en: The British do fire on Elsinore, don't they?
sentences.zh: 英国人确实向埃尔西诺开火了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because isn't there a cannonball stuck in the cathedral roof or something?
sentences.zh: 因为大教堂的屋顶上不是还嵌着一颗炮弹什么的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, apparently.
sentences.zh: 是的，好像是这样。

sentences.en: So on they go into the strait.
sentences.zh: 于是他们继续驶入海峡。

sentences.en: In the distance, 20 miles away is their target, the city of Copenhagen.
sentences.zh: 在20英里外的远方，就是他们的目标——哥本哈根市。

sentences.en: Now, for a couple of days, they remain at anchor.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们在那儿抛锚停泊了几天。

sentences.en: It's really, really cold.
sentences.zh: 天气真的非常非常冷。

sentences.en: The weather is terrible.
sentences.zh: 气候糟糕透了。

sentences.en: And Nelson sends these little scouting parties into what is called the Outer Deep, which is the sort of sea beyond just outside Copenhagen.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊派出了几支小侦察队进入所谓的“外深水区”，也就是哥本哈根外围的海域。

sentences.en: It's all very icy, so it's kind of floating ice.
sentences.zh: 到处都是冰，所以到处漂浮着冰块。

sentences.en: And they're kind of cutting their way through.
sentences.zh: 他们得一边切开冰块一边前进。

sentences.en: And their job is to check out the Danish defences.
sentences.zh: 他们的任务是查探丹麦的防御工事。

sentences.en: And they have to do it at night, don't they?
sentences.zh: 而且他们必须在夜间行动，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's very Hollywood, this.
sentences.zh: 没错，这很有好莱坞大片的既视感。

sentences.en: So kind of muffled oars, and they can only use candles to inspect their charts and things.
sentences.zh: 他们得把桨包起来减小声音，只能用蜡烛照明来查看海图之类的东西。

sentences.en: The amazing thing is, is that obviously this is the kind of adventure that Nelson is gagging to join in.
sentences.zh: 令人惊叹的是，这显然是纳尔逊那种渴望参与的冒险。

sentences.en: And so he himself, even though he's the commander, goes out and joins these routines as well.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管他是指挥官，他还是亲自出马，加入了这些例行侦察。

sentences.en: Very dramatic scene.
sentences.zh: 非常戏剧性的场景。

sentences.en: Yeah, he loves all this.
sentences.zh: 没错，他热爱这一切。

sentences.en: And if you remember from last time, he has been going through agonies in his cabin, writing these letters to Emma about his paranoia that she's going to run off with
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得上次的内容，他在船舱里备受煎熬，给艾玛写信，担心她会跟

sentences.en: the future George IV.
sentences.zh: 未来的乔治四世私奔。

sentences.en: But this is the one time where you feel like a lot of these cares slip away, because this is really what he loves doing.
sentences.zh: 但这是唯一一次你会觉得他放下了一切忧虑，因为这才是他真正热爱的事业。

sentences.en: He just loves throwing himself into this kind of adventuring.
sentences.zh: 他就是喜欢投身于这种冒险之中。

sentences.en: And also hanging out with his band of brothers.
sentences.zh: 还有和他的“兄弟连”待在一起。

sentences.en: Yeah, and there's still a band of brothers element to this.
sentences.zh: 没错，这里面依然有“兄弟连”的成分。

sentences.en: So on the night of the 31st, after dinner, he has a council of war aboard the Elephant.
sentences.zh: 所以在31号晚上，晚餐后，他在“象号”战舰上召开了作战会议。

sentences.en: And a lot of the captains who are coming with him on this expedition are people that he served alongside at the Battle of the Nile.
sentences.zh: 和他一起参加这次远征的许多船长，都是他在尼罗河海战中并肩作战过的战友。

sentences.en: So names like Thomas Foley, Thomas Fremantle, George Murray.
sentences.zh: 比如托马斯·福利、托马斯·弗里曼特尔、乔治·默里这些名字。

sentences.en: The most famous of them is Thomas Masterman Hardy, who actually volunteers to leave his own ship and come over to the Elephant because he's so keen to be in on the action.
sentences.zh: 其中最著名的是托马斯·马斯特曼·哈迪，他主动请缨离开自己的船，来到“象号”，因为他太想参与战斗了。

sentences.en: And in the last couple of episodes, we talked a lot about the downsides of working with Horatio
sentences.zh: 在过去几期节目中，我们谈了很多与霍雷肖·

sentences.en: Nelson.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊共事的弊端。

sentences.en: But this is a reminder of just how inspirational,
sentences.zh: 但这提醒了我们，他是多么鼓舞人心，

sentences.en: how stirring a figure he is, that there are people who want to put themselves in harm's way just to be at his side in the thick of
sentences.zh: 多么令人振奋的人物，以至于人们愿意为了站在他身边冲锋陷阵，而将自己置于险境。

sentences.en: the action.
sentences.zh: 身处战斗的最前线。

sentences.en: But it's the Nelson touch, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是“纳尔逊风格”，不是吗？

sentences.en: The sense that huge drama is going to happen and it's probably going to work out well.
sentences.zh: 那种预感会有大事发生，而且很可能会圆满解决的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah, and he is a man who's brilliant at bringing people into his confidence and inspiring them.
sentences.zh: 没错，他是一个非常擅长赢得他人信任并激励他人的人。

sentences.en: There are these sort of descriptions of him, this guy called Colonel Stuart, William Stuart, who's commanding the sort of ground troops they brought with them.
sentences.zh: 有关于他的描述，比如这位叫斯图尔特上校的威廉·斯图尔特，他指挥着他们带来的地面部队。

sentences.en: And Stuart describes Nelson afterwards as pacing up and down, shaking his head at any sign of alarm or irresolution, burning with excitement and energy as he describes his plan.
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特后来描述纳尔逊在甲板上踱步，对任何惊慌或犹豫的迹象都摇头表示不满，在描述计划时，他燃烧着兴奋和活力。

sentences.en: This is a preview of what he will do at Trafalgar, of course, sharing his plan with his captains.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是他后来在特拉法尔加海战中与船长们分享计划的预演。

sentences.en: Yeah, and he's brilliant at generating this kind of sense of a shared bond.
sentences.zh: 没错，他非常擅长营造这种纽带感。

sentences.en: I mean, almost a kind of a manly love that animates everybody in command under Nelson
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这几乎是一种激励了纳尔逊麾下所有指挥官的兄弟情谊，

sentences.en: to feel that they're part of a shared enterprise and that that enterprise is going to be something
sentences.zh: 让他们觉得他们是共同事业的一部分，而且这项事业将是

sentences.en: bold, something dramatic, and ultimately something successful that you simply wouldn't get with any other admiral.
sentences.zh: 大胆的、戏剧性的，最终是成功的，这是你在任何其他海军上将那里都无法得到的体验。

sentences.en: And a glaring contrast with Sir Hyde Parker, who's not part of this.
sentences.zh: 这与海德·帕克爵士形成了鲜明的对比，他并不参与其中。

sentences.en: I mean, he's kind of stuck in the rear.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他被困在后方。

sentences.en: He's absolutely not the kind of person who could marshal this kind of project.
sentences.zh: 他绝对不是那种能统筹这种项目的人。

sentences.en: No, exactly.
sentences.zh: 不，确实如此。

sentences.en: And in fact, he's quite nervous about it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他对此感到非常紧张。

sentences.en: Well, he's nervous because it's a very risky plan.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他紧张是因为这是一个风险极高的计划。

sentences.en: Basically, what they're going to do is they're going to sail into Copenhagen harbour from the southeaSt.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们要做的是从东南方驶入哥本哈根港。

sentences.en: And to do that, they'll have to loop around this central sort of shoal or sandbank known as the middle ground.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，他们必须绕过被称为“中间地带”的中央浅滩或沙洲。

sentences.en: And if they loop around that and come up from the south, that will bring them into what's called the King's Deep, which is this quite narrow channel between the shoal and the city.
sentences.zh: 如果他们绕过那里从南面驶入，就会进入所谓的“国王深水区”，这是浅滩和城市之间一条相当狭窄的航道。

sentences.en: But it is, as its name suggests, deep.
sentences.zh: 但正如其名，它确实很深。

sentences.en: Because I suppose the risk is that, I mean, it's exactly the risk that Nelson faced at the Battle of the Nile, where similarly there were kind of shoals and islands and sandbanks
sentences.zh: 因为我想风险在于，这正是纳尔逊在尼罗河海战中面临的风险，那里同样有各种浅滩、岛屿和沙洲

sentences.en: and so on.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: And listeners may remember that one of the most celebrated of all Nelson's captains, Thomas
sentences.zh: 听众可能还记得，纳尔逊最著名的船长之一，托马斯·

sentences.en: Trowbridge, ends up stranded there.
sentences.zh: 特鲁布里奇，最终在那里搁浅了。

sentences.en: And he's terribly upset about this.
sentences.zh: 他对此感到非常难过。

sentences.en: And Nelson has to push for him to get a medal, even though he hadn't taken part in the fight.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊不得不力排众议为他争取勋章，尽管他没能参加战斗。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there is absolutely a risk, because actually the channel here, the deep, is even narrower than it had been in Egypt, that people will get stranded similarly.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是有风险的，因为这里的航道比埃及那会儿还要窄，人们同样会搁浅。

sentences.en: However, Nelson has made this less likely by having the shoals marked out with boys, because
sentences.zh: 然而，纳尔逊通过用浮标标出浅滩，降低了这种可能性，因为

sentences.en: normally there would be boys there, but the Danes have removed the boys to make it more challenging for the British.
sentences.zh: 正常情况下那里会有浮标，但丹麦人移走了浮标，想给英国人制造更多麻烦。

sentences.en: And he has a splendid man, a splendid officer who he entrusts with this task.
sentences.zh: 他有一位出色的部下，一位他委以重任的出色军官。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Captain Edward Ryu, who's a very junior officer, but has had an amazing career.
sentences.zh: 这就是爱德华·里奥船长，他虽然资历尚浅，但职业生涯非常惊人。

sentences.en: So he'd been a midshipman on Cook's third and final voyage, the voyage in which Captain
sentences.zh: 他曾是库克船长第三次也是最后一次航行中的见习船员，那次航行中库克

sentences.en: Cook ends up being killed in Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 船长最终在夏威夷被杀。

sentences.en: There'd been massive drama with a convict ship that he'd been in command of.
sentences.zh: 他指挥的一艘运送囚犯的船曾发生过巨大的变故。

sentences.en: He was taking prisoners to Botany Bay, and they had tried to get water from an iceberg, and the iceberg had sliced a hole in the bottom of the ship.
sentences.zh: 他当时正要把囚犯送往植物学湾，他们试图从冰山上取水，结果冰山在船底撞出了一个洞。

sentences.en: And they kept trying to bail the water out.
sentences.zh: 他们一直试图把水舀出去。

sentences.en: And some of the crew say, oh, this is hopeless.
sentences.zh: 一些船员说，噢，这没希望了。

sentences.en: We're getting out of here.
sentences.zh: 我们得离开这儿。

sentences.en: And they go off in ships.
sentences.zh: 于是他们乘船逃走了。

sentences.en: But Ryu stays on board, and he uses the convicts as a crew.
sentences.zh: 但里奥留在了船上，他让囚犯们充当船员。

sentences.en: So it's almost the opposite of Bly.
sentences.zh: 这几乎和布莱船长的遭遇相反。

sentences.en: Bly had lost his crew.
sentences.zh: 布莱失去了他的船员。

sentences.en: Ryu recruits convicts to serve him as his crew.
sentences.zh: 里奥招募囚犯来为他服务。

sentences.en: And somehow they manage to survive, and they get rescued.
sentences.zh: 他们竟然奇迹般地活了下来，并获救了。

sentences.en: I don't know if you've read Desolation Island.
sentences.zh: 不知道你有没有读过《荒凉岛》。

sentences.en: Of course, Patrick O'Brien.
sentences.zh: 当然，帕特里克·奥布莱恩的作品。

sentences.en: So this is exactly the plot of that.
sentences.zh: 所以这正是书中的情节。

sentences.en: It's a direct inspiration for it.
sentences.zh: 这是它的直接灵感来源。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's an amazing scene in Patrick O'Brien.
sentences.zh: 没错，帕特里克·奥布莱恩书中的那个场景太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so there's something of Jack Aubrey, Patrick O'Brien's hero, about Captain Ryu.
sentences.zh: 所以里奥船长身上确实有帕特里克·奥布莱恩笔下的英雄杰克·奥布里的影子。

sentences.en: And you can see exactly why that would appeal to Nelson.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出为什么这会吸引纳尔逊。

sentences.en: And so he has given Ryu not command of a kind of major ship of the line, but of a small squadron of frigates.
sentences.zh: 所以他给里奥的不是一艘主力舰的指挥权，而是一支小型护卫舰中队。

sentences.en: And he gives him a kind of roving commission in the battle to come, you know, if kind of happenstance intervenes, if things go wrong.
sentences.zh: 他在即将到来的战斗中给了他一种“游击”的使命，你知道，如果发生意外，如果事情出了差错。

sentences.en: Ryu is to rely on his initiative and basically behave as Nelson likes to behave in battles.
sentences.zh: 里奥要依靠自己的主动性，基本上表现得像纳尔逊在战斗中喜欢表现的那样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's how they're getting around the sandbanks or the shoals.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们绕过沙洲或浅滩的方法。

sentences.en: But once they've done that, they're then into the harbour, and there's this line of
sentences.zh: 但一旦他们做到了，他们就进入了港口，那里有一排

sentences.en: Danish ships.
sentences.zh: 丹麦军舰。

sentences.en: Now here, they really have to take a gamble.
sentences.zh: 在这里，他们真的必须赌一把。

sentences.en: Each of Nelson's ships is given a different target, and they kind of move up the line towards their targets, one by one.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊的每艘船都被分配了不同的目标，他们一个接一个地向目标推进。

sentences.en: And they keep going till they've cleared them all out of the way.
sentences.zh: 他们会一直打到把所有障碍清除为止。

sentences.en: And Nelson says, when you do this, the Danes will be absolutely, you know, there'll be a blizzard of Danish fire.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊说，当你这样做时，丹麦人会绝对，你知道，会有一场丹麦人的炮火暴风雪。

sentences.en: But we should get, quote, so close to our enemies that every shot cannot miss.
sentences.zh: 但我们应该，引用他的话，“如此靠近我们的敌人，以至于每一发炮弹都不会落空”。

sentences.en: Let's give them that hailstorm of bullets, which gives our dear country the dominion of the seas.
sentences.zh: 让我们给他们那场冰雹般的炮火，这将为我们亲爱的国家赢得海洋的统治权。

sentences.en: That's very Nelson.
sentences.zh: 这非常纳尔逊。

sentences.en: And that's why the carinades are so useful in such a fight.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么短管炮在这样的战斗中如此有用。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Plus, getting up really close.
sentences.zh: 再加上，靠得非常近。

sentences.en: So you advance closer and closer in the face of their withering fire, and then you just unload and unleash hell on them.
sentences.zh: 所以你在他们猛烈的炮火下越靠越近，然后你就尽情倾泻炮火，释放地狱般的攻击。

sentences.en: So you've got to be pretty brave.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须非常勇敢。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We come to the morning of the 1st of April.
sentences.zh: 我们来到4月1日的早晨。

sentences.en: The wind has begun to shift in their favor.
sentences.zh: 风向开始向有利于他们的方向转变。

sentences.en: Nelson calls the masters and the pilots of the ships for a last briefing on the elephant.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊召集了各舰的船长和领航员在“象号”上进行最后一次简报。

sentences.en: Then he himself gets into a little rowing boat, and he goes to visit as many ships as he can.
sentences.zh: 然后他自己坐上一艘小划艇，去拜访尽可能多的船只。

sentences.en: And there's a midshipman who remembers.
sentences.zh: 有一位见习船员记得。

sentences.en: He says, I always remember Nelson.
sentences.zh: 他说，我永远记得纳尔逊。

sentences.en: His squeaking little voice in his Norfolk drawl.
sentences.zh: 他那尖细的嗓音和诺福克口音。

sentences.en: Alan Partridge.
sentences.zh: 艾伦·帕特里奇。

sentences.en: Alan Partridge.
sentences.zh: 艾伦·帕特里奇。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: So they start to move south that afternoon.
sentences.zh: 于是那天下午他们开始向南移动。

sentences.en: When they see the signal to begin the operation, great cheers rise from the crews.
sentences.zh: 当他们看到开始行动的信号时，船员们爆发出巨大的欢呼声。

sentences.en: And in the distance, of course, they can now see the spires of Copenhagen, and they can also make out the outline of the defensive line across the harbor, this wall of guns.
sentences.zh: 在远处，当然，他们现在可以看到哥本哈根的尖塔，也能辨认出横跨港口的防御线轮廓，那是一堵炮火之墙。

sentences.en: And as dusk is falling, we have that scene that you opened with, Tom, I described in such purple prose.
sentences.zh: 当暮色降临时，我们有了汤姆你开场时描述的那个场景，我用如此华丽的辞藻描述过。

sentences.en: Stirring prose, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 令人振奋的文笔，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Thanks, Tom.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，汤姆。

sentences.en: Honestly, I read it and I felt a thrill.

sentences.zh: 他脱离了战线，发起了一次单人任务，基本上改变了整个战局。

sentences.en: He had gone out of the line, and he had sort of launched this solo mission that basically changed the whole course of the battle.
sentences.zh: 所以有时候，你知道，当他坚持自己的判断时，是有回报的。

sentences.en: So sometimes, you know, when he backs his own judgment, it pays off.
sentences.zh: 所以他只花了一会儿时间，然后嘟囔道。

sentences.en: So it takes him just a moment, and he mutters.
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特上校听到他低声嘟囔：“停止战斗？”

sentences.en: Colonel Stewart hears him mutter under his breath, leave off action.
sentences.zh: “不，我才不干呢。”

sentences.en: No, damn me if I do.
sentences.zh: 一位中尉问：“我们要重复这个信号吗？”

sentences.en: And a lieutenant says, shall we repeat the signal?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就是把信号传达给其余的船只。

sentences.en: In other words, transmit the signal to the rest of our ships.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊说：“确认收到，但不要重复。”

sentences.en: Nelson says, acknowledge it, but do not repeat it.
sentences.zh: “保持16号信号悬挂。”

sentences.en: Keep signal 16 aloft.
sentences.zh: 那是那个信号。

sentences.en: That is the signal.
sentences.zh: “更近距离地与敌人交战。”

sentences.en: Engage the enemy more closely.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，它反映了纳尔逊的自信，即他认为自己对战线的掌控力比名义上的总司令还要强。

sentences.en: And the thing about that is, it's reflective of Nelson's confidence that he has more authority over the line of battle than the ostensible commander-in-chief does.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我们将看看他是否真的有理由如此自信。

sentences.en: And we will see if he's right to be that confident.
sentences.zh: 现在，后甲板上的其他人知道这是公然抗命。

sentences.en: Now, the other men on the quarterdeck know that this is rank in subordination.
sentences.zh: 我认为很明显，福里船长对此感到震惊，因为他实际上似乎是在寻求确认。

sentences.en: I think it's pretty clear that Captain Foley is shocked by it because he effectively seems to ask for confirmation.
sentences.zh: “您确定吗，长官？”

sentences.en: Are you sure, sir?
sentences.zh: 或者类似的话。

sentences.en: Or something along those lines.
sentences.zh: 或者他只是挑了挑眉毛。

sentences.en: Or maybe he just raises an eyebrow.
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 现在，接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Now, what happens next?
sentences.zh: 这就是每个英国学童过去常学的故事。

sentences.en: Here is the story that every British schoolchild used to learn.
sentences.zh: 而且现在也应该学。

sentences.en: And still should.
sentences.zh: 绝对应该。

sentences.en: Absolutely, they should.
sentences.zh: 说实话。

sentences.en: Let's be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊对福里说：“你知道，福里，我只有一只眼睛。”

sentences.en: Nelson says to Foley, you know, Foley, I have only one eye.
sentences.zh: “我有权偶尔装瞎。”

sentences.en: I have a right to be blind sometimes.
sentences.zh: 我有权偶尔装瞎。

sentences.en: And then, a great gesture, pure Nelsonian theater.
sentences.zh: 接着，一个伟大的姿态，纯粹的纳尔逊式戏剧表演。

sentences.en: He reaches for a telescope and he puts it to his sightless eye, the one that can't see.
sentences.zh: 他伸手去拿望远镜，把它放在自己那只失明的眼睛上，那只什么也看不见的眼睛。

sentences.en: And he says, I really do not see the signal.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，我真的没看见那个信号。

sentences.en: Now, the sad thing about this story is that some of Nelson's biographers, I'm sorry to say, let themselves down by doubting it.
sentences.zh: 这个故事令人遗憾的一点是，很抱歉地说，纳尔逊的一些传记作者竟然怀疑它的真实性，这真让人失望。

sentences.en: Isn't that right?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: I don't think it's sad because I think it's up there with, you know, Alfred burning the cakes.
sentences.zh: 我不觉得这有什么好遗憾的，因为我觉得这和阿尔弗雷德烧焦蛋糕的故事处于同一水平，你知道的。

sentences.en: Of course it is.
sentences.zh: 当然是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Robert the Bruce and the spider.
sentences.zh: 还有罗伯特·布鲁斯和蜘蛛的故事。

sentences.en: It's Drake and the Armada.
sentences.zh: 还有德雷克和无敌舰队的故事。

sentences.en: So, the Armada arrives and Drake's playing a game of bowls and he says, it's time to finish the game and beat the Armada too.
sentences.zh: 当时，无敌舰队抵达了，德雷克正在玩草地滚球，他说，是时候结束比赛，顺便击败无敌舰队了。

sentences.en: And he does.
sentences.zh: 他也确实做到了。

sentences.en: And the thing is that all these stories, they have the power that they do because they're very dramatic, but also because they illustrate the truth of the circumstances.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，所有这些故事之所以有如此大的影响力，是因为它们非常戏剧化，同时也因为它们阐明了当时环境的真相。

sentences.en: We've done Greek myths.
sentences.zh: 我们已经讲过希腊神话了。

sentences.en: I mean, myths have a power that isn't directly dependent on whether they are factually true or not.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，神话的力量并不直接取决于它们在事实上是否真实。

sentences.en: However, of course, historians are going to scoff at this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 然而，历史学家当然会对这类事情嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: But equally, there are those who say, well, you know, I think it's more likely this happened than that Alfred burnt his cakes, for instance.
sentences.zh: 但同样地，也有人会说，嗯，你知道，我觉得这比阿尔弗雷德烧焦蛋糕的事情更有可能发生。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And actually, John Sugden, who spent an enormous amount of ink on this particular story, looking at the provenance of it, all the different accounts.
sentences.zh: 事实上，约翰·萨格登在这一特定故事上花费了大量笔墨，研究了它的起源和各种不同的记载。

sentences.en: So, basically, Colonel Stewart told his story about what happened on the quarterdeck several times in the next 10 years or so.
sentences.zh: 基本上，斯图尔特上校在接下来的十年左右里，多次讲述了他在后甲板上发生的事情。

sentences.en: And as so often with anecdotes, the anecdotes slightly changed in each telling.
sentences.zh: 正如轶事中经常出现的那样，这些轶事在每次讲述时都会略有变化。

sentences.en: Improved, what might I say?
sentences.zh: 可以说，是润色了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it improved.
sentences.zh: 是的，润色了。

sentences.en: But Sugden says, listen, you can doubt it and you can say, well, the very, very earliest stories about what happened on the quarterdeck don't mention it.
sentences.zh: 但萨格登说，听着，你可以怀疑它，你可以说，关于后甲板上发生的事情，最早的那些故事里并没有提到这一点。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that it didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着它没有发生。

sentences.en: Does it have the ring of implausibility?
sentences.zh: 它听起来不可信吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds perfectly plausible, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来完全合情合理，对吧？

sentences.en: That's the key.
sentences.zh: 这才是关键。

sentences.en: So, Sugden says, the telescope story is entirely in Nelson's character.
sentences.zh: 所以，萨格登说，望远镜的故事完全符合纳尔逊的性格。

sentences.en: He never forgot his audience.
sentences.zh: 他从不忘记他的观众。

sentences.en: And that could either mean that people assume it's true because it sounds right.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着人们认为它是真的，因为它听起来很对劲。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But equally, it could be true because Nelson would do it.
sentences.zh: 但同样地，它也可能是真的，因为纳尔逊确实会那么做。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the one thing that's definitely not true is the kind of thing that you will often see on illustrations of this scene that shows Nelson raising his telescope to
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得有一点绝对不是真的，那就是你经常在这一场景的插图中看到的，纳尔逊把望远镜举到

sentences.en: an eyepatch.
sentences.zh: 眼罩上。

sentences.en: And we have already emphasized Nelson did not wear a kind of pirate eyepatch.
sentences.zh: 我们已经强调过，纳尔逊并没有戴那种海盗眼罩。

sentences.en: But I think we've concluded, haven't we, Tom, that it absolutely happened.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们已经达成共识了，不是吗，汤姆？这件事绝对发生了。

sentences.en: And in many ways, it happened more bravely than people have given Nelson credit for.
sentences.zh: 而且在许多方面，这件事发生得比人们给予纳尔逊的赞誉更为勇敢。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我也这么认为。

sentences.en: So, he's taken this incredible risk.
sentences.zh: 所以，他冒了难以置信的风险。

sentences.en: And actually, here is the ultimate demonstration of Nelson's reputation among his fellow captains.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这正是纳尔逊在各位舰长中享有崇高声望的终极证明。

sentences.en: Everybody follows his lead.
sentences.zh: 每个人都追随他的领导。

sentences.en: None of the other warship captains question him.
sentences.zh: 其他战舰舰长中没有一个人质疑他。

sentences.en: None of them break off the attack.
sentences.zh: 没有一个人中断进攻。

sentences.en: Of course, in that case, they would be disobeying Nelson.
sentences.zh: 当然，在这种情况下，他们就是在违抗纳尔逊。

sentences.en: And there's no recrimination afterwards.
sentences.zh: 而且事后也没有任何指责。

sentences.en: There is one captain who does obey Parker's orders, and this is Edward Ryu, who Nelson particularly admires.
sentences.zh: 有一位舰长确实服从了帕克的命令，他就是爱德华·里尤，纳尔逊特别钦佩他。

sentences.en: He's shown a great initiative.
sentences.zh: 他展现了极大的主动性。

sentences.en: He's gone to the top of the line.
sentences.zh: 他已经冲到了战列的最前方。

sentences.en: But he is a very, very junior officer.
sentences.zh: 但他只是一名非常、非常低级的军官。

sentences.en: It's a massive, massive deal for him, much more than for Nelson's more established captains to break an order.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，违抗命令是一件非常、非常重大的事情，远比对纳尔逊那些资深舰长来说要严重得多。

sentences.en: And so, he very, very reluctantly gives his squadron of five ships the order to withdraw.
sentences.zh: 所以，他非常、非常不情愿地向他的五艘舰艇组成的编队下达了撤退命令。

sentences.en: I mean, he keeps on fighting for half an hour, but ultimately, he thinks, you know, I've been given a direct order.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他继续战斗了半小时，但最终他想，你知道，我接到了直接命令。

sentences.en: I've got to obey it.
sentences.zh: 我必须服从它。

sentences.en: And you were saying how, had Nelson ordered a withdrawal, this would have been calamitous for the entire British line.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到，如果纳尔逊下令撤退，这对整个英国战列来说将是灾难性的。

sentences.en: And the fate of Ryu illustrates this.
sentences.zh: 而里尤的命运就说明了这一点。

sentences.en: Because what happens is that as his squadron of frigates starts to turn and withdraw and stop firing, the gun smoke clears.
sentences.zh: 因为当他的护卫舰编队开始转向撤退并停止射击时，炮烟散去了。

sentences.en: And Ryu's own ship, which is the last to withdraw, you know, there is no disguise now.
sentences.zh: 而里尤自己的船，作为最后一艘撤退的船，你知道，现在没有任何掩护了。

sentences.en: It's open fire for the Danish gunners.
sentences.zh: 这对丹麦炮手来说是公开的靶子。

sentences.en: And we have an account from Colonel Stewart, you know, who was with Nelson, who may or may not have seen him putting his telescope to his blind eye, who describes what happened.
sentences.zh: 我们有斯图尔特上校的记载，你知道，他当时和纳尔逊在一起，他可能看到了也可能没看到纳尔逊把望远镜放在失明的眼睛上，他描述了发生的事情。

sentences.en: So, this is Stewart on Ryu.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是斯图尔特关于里尤的描述。

sentences.en: He had expressed himself grieved at being obliged to retreat and nobly observed, what will
sentences.zh: 他曾表示对被迫撤退感到悲痛，并高尚地感叹道，纳尔逊会

sentences.en: Nelson think of us?
sentences.zh: 怎么看我们？

sentences.en: His clerk was killed by his side.
sentences.zh: 他的书记员在他身边被杀死了。

sentences.en: And by another shot, several Marines, while hauling on the main brace, shared the same fate.
sentences.zh: 另一发炮弹击中了几名正在拉主索的海军陆战队员，他们也遭遇了同样的命运。

sentences.en: Ryu then exclaimed, come then, my boys, let us all die together.
sentences.zh: 里尤随后惊呼，来吧，小伙子们，让我们一起战死吧。

sentences.en: The words were scarcely uttered when the fatal shot severed him in two.
sentences.zh: 话音刚落，致命的炮弹就将他拦腰截断。

sentences.en: So, that's very moving.
sentences.zh: 这真是太感人了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: How does Colonel Stewart know, by the way, because he's on a different ship?
sentences.zh: 顺便问一下，斯图尔特上校是怎么知道的？因为他在另一艘船上。

sentences.en: I imagine that it's reported to him.
sentences.zh: 我想是有人向他报告的。

sentences.en: Listen, I'm never going to be sceptical about a story like this.
sentences.zh: 听着，我永远不会对这样的故事持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, again, what will Nelson think of us?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，再说一次，纳尔逊会怎么看我们？

sentences.en: Come then, my boys, let us all die together.
sentences.zh: 来吧，小伙子们，让我们一起战死吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, you might think these phrases are too good to be true, but I think it's striking that Ryu is a particular favourite of Nelson's.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可能会觉得这些话好得不像真的，但我认为引人注目的是，里尤是纳尔逊特别喜爱的人。

sentences.en: He's only met him on the course of this expedition.
sentences.zh: 他只是在这次远征的过程中才认识他。

sentences.en: Clearly, there is a kind of self-dramatising quality to Ryu's heroism that Nelson really identifies with.
sentences.zh: 显然，里尤的英雄主义中有一种自我戏剧化的特质，纳尔逊对此深有共鸣。

sentences.en: So, again, I think it's perfectly plausible he said that.
sentences.zh: 所以，再说一次，我觉得他说过那番话是完全合理的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Just like the telescope.
sentences.zh: 就像望远镜那件事一样。

sentences.en: The self-dramatising is driven from the top.
sentences.zh: 这种自我戏剧化是从高层传导下来的。

sentences.en: You have a man who is constructing his life as though he's on the stage, I would say.
sentences.zh: 你会发现有一个人，他构建自己的人生就像是在舞台上一样，我会这么说。

sentences.en: And so, other people follow suit.
sentences.zh: 所以，其他人也纷纷效仿。

sentences.en: And Nelson says that Ryu's loss is almost the worst loss of the battle, you know, that he would have gone on to really great things.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊说，里尤的牺牲几乎是这场战斗中最惨重的损失，你知道，他本可以成就一番伟业的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, back at the harbour, it's about two o'clock.
sentences.zh: 回到港口，大约是两点钟。

sentences.en: Huge, great clouds of black smoke.
sentences.zh: 巨大的黑色烟云。

sentences.en: The air is thick with kind of screams and explosions.
sentences.zh: 空气中弥漫着尖叫声和爆炸声。

sentences.en: The Danes are fighting manfully, but they're in real trouble now.
sentences.zh: 丹麦人英勇作战，但他们现在陷入了真正的困境。

sentences.en: By about two o'clock, the Danabrog, their flagship, is burning.
sentences.zh: 大约两点钟，他们的旗舰“丹内布罗格号”正在燃烧。

sentences.en: By about 2.30, its gun crews have been completely slaughtered and the flag comes down and the survivors have to flee for the shore.
sentences.zh: 大约两点半，它的炮手被彻底屠杀，旗帜降下，幸存者不得不逃往岸边。

sentences.en: The Danish commander is a bloke called Commodore Olfert Fischer.
sentences.zh: 丹麦指挥官是一个叫奥尔费特·费舍尔准将的人。

sentences.en: And he's already moved his flag to another ship, the Holston.
sentences.zh: 他已经把旗帜移到了另一艘船“霍尔斯顿号”上。

sentences.en: About the same time, that ship's overpowered as well.
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时间，那艘船也被压制了。

sentences.en: And he has to take refuge in one of the forts, the Trek-on-Earth fort.
sentences.zh: 他不得不躲进其中一个堡垒，特雷克罗纳堡垒。

sentences.en: So, it's very clear the British have the upper hand.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，英国人占据了上风。

sentences.en: They don't have things entirely their own way, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，他们并没有完全掌控局面。

sentences.en: I mean, this is still a really, you know, this is what makes Nelson's call so dicey, is that it's still pretty tight.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这仍然是一个，你知道，这就是为什么纳尔逊的决定如此冒险的原因，因为局势依然非常紧张。

sentences.en: And, you know, some of his ships, the Monarch and the Defiance, are really taking terrible, terrible punishment.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他的一些船只，比如“君主号”和“反抗号”，正在遭受极其惨重的打击。

sentences.en: The Danish batteries are still intact.
sentences.zh: 丹麦的炮台依然完好无损。

sentences.en: They're still firing relentlessly.
sentences.zh: 它们仍在无情地开火。

sentences.en: And now I think Nelson does one of the most impressive things he ever did in a battle.
sentences.zh: 现在我认为纳尔逊做了他在战斗中所做过的最令人印象深刻的事情之一。

sentences.en: Because he's not just about get up close and batter them and then we'll win.
sentences.zh: 因为他不仅仅是想靠近并猛轰他们，然后我们就能赢。

sentences.en: He's also thinking politically.
sentences.zh: 他也在进行政治思考。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's an Achilles, but he's a calculating Achilles.
sentences.zh: 他是一位阿喀琉斯，但他是精于算计的阿喀琉斯。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, he goes down below for a second and he scribbles a note that is basically offering the Danes a deal.
sentences.zh: 所以，他下到甲板下片刻，草拟了一张字条，基本上是向丹麦人提供了一项协议。

sentences.en: And then he gives it to a bloke called Frederick Thesiger, who speaks Danish, and says, can you get in a little boat, go over to the shore under a flag of truce,
sentences.zh: 然后他把它交给了一个叫弗雷德里克·西西格的人，他会说丹麦语，并说，你能坐上一艘小船，在休战旗帜下前往岸边吗？

sentences.en: find Crown Prince Frederick and give him this note.
sentences.zh: 找到王储弗雷德里克并把这张字条交给他。

sentences.en: And Crown Prince Frederick is George III's nephew.
sentences.zh: 而王储弗雷德里克是乔治三世的侄子。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, there are certain familial bonds.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他们之间存在某种亲缘关系。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, why did Nelson do this?
sentences.zh: 那么，纳尔逊为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: Afterwards, he always said, I did it because basically I'm a very kind person and I wanted to spare the Danes any more bloodshed.
sentences.zh: 事后，他总是说，我这么做基本上是因为我是一个非常善良的人，我想让丹麦人免受更多的流血。

sentences.en: But, you know, Dominic, I think that's true.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，多米尼克，我觉得那是真的。

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds counterintuitive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来有悖常理。

sentences.zh: 我们的国家生存取决于我们能否，你知道，实施这些封锁。

sentences.zh: 这是我们对抗法国人的唯一途径。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，法国人比那更具威胁性。

sentences.en: But the issue for the Danes remains that the Russians are much closer than the British.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, the French are even more menacing than that.
sentences.zh: 丹麦人想要贸易，想要做所有这些事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 所以谈判持续了几天。

sentences.en: And the Danes want to trade and they want to do all this.
sentences.zh: 事实上时间太长了，纳尔逊甚至能溜去皇家哥本哈根瓷器公司，为艾玛订购了一套餐具。

sentences.en: So the talks, they go on for a few days.
sentences.zh: 所以，他再次专注于核心问题。

sentences.en: So long, in fact, that Nelson is able to bunk off to the Royal Copenhagen Porcelain Company, where he orders a dinner service for Emma.
sentences.zh: 然后在谈判的第六天，也就是4月8日，那是个糟糕的日子，大雨倾盆，非常凄惨。

sentences.en: So again, he's laser focused on the main issues.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当纳尔逊和他的官员们到达宫殿时，他们浑身湿透，不得不站在火炉旁烤了很久，把衣服烘干才能被带去参加会议。

sentences.en: And then on the sixth day of talks, which is the 8th of April, it's a terrible day, pouring rain, very miserable.

sentences.en: Actually, when Nelson and his officials turn up at the palace, they're so bedraggled, they have to stand by the fire for ages to dry out before they can be shown into the meeting.
sentences.zh: 未来几个月我们将保持中立。

sentences.en: They get in and the crown prince says, okay, fine, we've got a deal.
sentences.zh: 这会给你时间去对付俄国人。

sentences.en: We will remain neutral for the next few months.
sentences.zh: 作为交换，我们将为你补给和重新装载船只等等。

sentences.en: That'll give you time to deal with the Russians.
sentences.zh: 你必须全部从我们这里购买。

sentences.en: Now, in return, we will resupply you and restock your ships and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们很乐意这样做。

sentences.en: Nelson says, brilliant.

sentences.en: What a great deal this is.
sentences.zh: 这真是一笔划算的交易。

sentences.en: Now, only afterwards does he find out why they've come to the deal, because they know something that he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 然而，他直到事后才明白他们为何达成这笔交易，因为他们知道一些他所不知道的事情。

sentences.en: Bombshell news.

sentences.zh: 他是个非常古怪且令人反感的人，执着于人们穿错帽子、背心之类的琐事。

sentences.zh: 他们闯入了他位于圣彼得堡圣迈克尔城堡的公寓。

sentences.zh: 他们把他逼到了卧室的角落里。

sentences.zh: 他当时正躲在窗帘后面。

sentences.en: They dragged him out.

sentences.zh: 事实上，他的继任者亚历山大一世在拿破仑战争中多次倒戈，他上任后的首要举措之一就是与英国讲和。

sentences.en: A good start to the rain.
sentences.zh: 统治的良好开端。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Sensible policies for a happier Russia.
sentences.zh: 为了一个更幸福的俄罗斯，采取明智的政策。

sentences.en: So, all's well that ends well.
sentences.zh: 所以，结局好一切都好。

sentences.en: There's only one person who's slightly down in the dumps.
sentences.zh: 只有一个人稍微有点闷闷不乐。

sentences.zh: 猜猜那是谁？

sentences.en: It is, of course, Nelson.
sentences.zh: 当然是纳尔逊。

sentences.en: Is he complaining about how ill he feels?
sentences.zh: 他是在抱怨自己感觉有多不舒服吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 他立刻陷入了极度的自怜和疑病症中，抱怨头痛、眼睛不适以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, to be fair to him, it's not quite over yet because when the deal is done with the Danes, he doesn't know that the Russians are about to pull out.
sentences.zh: 我是说，平心而论，事情还没完全结束，因为当与丹麦人的交易达成时，他并不知道俄国人即将退出。

sentences.zh: 他最终成为了英国舰队的总司令，因为可怜的老海德·帕克爵士被召回了，因为他给纳尔逊下达命令的消息传了出去，人们

sentences.zh: 责怪他下达了命令，而不是责怪纳尔逊违抗命令。

sentences.zh: 不得不说，纳尔逊表现得非常得体。

sentences.zh: 他总是喜欢讲故事，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 但当纳尔逊寻找瑞典人时，我们听到了纳尔逊最精彩的故事之一，这个故事实际上在彼得·威尔的电影《怒海争锋》中重现了。

sentences.en: So, he's out in a little boat, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他当时是在一艘小船上，对吧？

sentences.zh: 那艘船来自“博洛尼亚”号，他们正在寻找瑞典人。

sentences.en: And the master of the boat said afterwards, it was extremely cold and I wished him to put on a great coat of mine, which was in the boat.
sentences.zh: 船长事后说，当时非常冷，我希望他穿上我的一件大衣，那件大衣就在船上。

sentences.en: And Nelson said to him, no, I am not cold.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊对他说，不，我不冷。

sentences.zh: 我对国家的焦虑会让我保持温暖。

sentences.zh: 在电影里，那是对国王和国家的赤诚之心。

sentences.zh: 罗素·克劳说，如果换作别人，你会说这太矫情了。

sentences.zh: 但对于纳尔逊，你会相信这是真的。

sentences.zh: 你感到内心深受触动。

sentences.zh: 看，这太精彩了。

sentences.zh: 但这对纳尔逊来说太疯狂了，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's great stuff that we can laugh about it now.
sentences.zh: 现在能拿这件事当笑谈真是太好了。

sentences.en: But at the time, he nearly dies because he's got this fever.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，他差点因为发烧而死。

sentences.en: He's coughing so badly that everyone thinks he's got TB.
sentences.zh: 他咳嗽得太厉害，以至于大家都以为他得了肺结核。

sentences.en: He's having what he calls heart strokes.
sentences.zh: 他出现了他所谓的“心脏病发作”。

sentences.en: Hard to work out what these are.
sentences.zh: 很难弄清楚那到底是什么。

sentences.en: They're almost like panic attacks, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想那更像是恐慌发作。

sentences.en: Palpitations or something, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我猜是心悸之类的吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And his officers are really worried about him.
sentences.zh: 他的军官们真的很担心他。

sentences.en: And actually, when people go back to London, they say, you've got to recall Nelson from the Baltic.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当人们回到伦敦时，他们说，你必须把纳尔逊从波罗的海召回来。

sentences.en: I mean, if you leave him out there, he will die.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你让他留在那里，他会死的。

sentences.en: Well, it's funny because the Earl of St. Vincent, so to Sir John Jervis, who knows Nelson obviously incredibly well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有趣，因为圣文森特伯爵，也就是约翰·杰维斯爵士，显然非常了解纳尔逊。

sentences.en: When these reports that Nelson's ill arrive in London, to begin with, he says absolutely nothing to worry about.
sentences.zh: 当这些关于纳尔逊生病的报告传到伦敦时，起初，他说完全不用担心。

sentences.en: So he tells the king, Nelson is always in the habit of complaining of ill health, you know, with the implication, just ignore it.
sentences.zh: 所以他告诉国王，纳尔逊一向有抱怨身体不适的习惯，你知道，言下之意就是，别理他。

sentences.en: And then a week later, the reports are so serious that he becomes alarmed too.
sentences.zh: 然后一周后，报告变得如此严重，以至于他也感到惊慌了。

sentences.en: And wheels are set in motion and Nelson is brought back.
sentences.zh: 于是行动开始，纳尔逊被带了回来。

sentences.en: So the orders reach him in Midsommar.
sentences.zh: 命令在仲夏时分传达到了他那里。

sentences.en: And by the 29th of July, he lands in Yarmouth once again, greeted by huge crowds, ringing bells, all of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 到7月29日，他再次在雅茅斯登陆，受到大批人群的欢迎，钟声齐鸣，诸如此类。

sentences.en: It's actually quite similar to the scene nine months earlier when he landed with the Hamiltons.
sentences.zh: 这实际上和九个月前他与汉密尔顿夫妇一起登陆时的场景非常相似。

sentences.en: The difference is there was a huge shadow that time.
sentences.zh: 不同之处在于，那次笼罩着巨大的阴影。

sentences.en: And there isn't the same shadow this time.
sentences.zh: 而这次没有同样的阴影。

sentences.en: I mean, Emma is waiting for him.
sentences.zh: 我是说，艾玛在等着他。

sentences.en: And of course, this saga, the Emma Fanny saga is not quite over.
sentences.zh: 当然，这个传奇，艾玛与范妮的传奇还没有完全结束。

sentences.en: You know, Nelson, Emma has been on his mind every minute of every day, hasn't she?
sentences.zh: 你知道，纳尔逊，艾玛每时每刻都在他的脑海里，不是吗？

sentences.en: And he's sent her tons of presents.
sentences.zh: 他给她寄了无数的礼物。

sentences.en: Well, he's got all that porcelain set from Copenhagen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他有从哥本哈根买的那套瓷器。

sentences.zh: 瓷器，几瓶酒，丹麦酒。

sentences.en: That's an odd...
sentences.zh: 那真是个奇怪的……

sentences.zh: 是啊，那……

sentences.en: Now, sad to say, poor Fanny, Nelson's wife, has not quite given up hope of winning him back.
sentences.zh: 现在，令人遗憾的是，可怜的范妮，纳尔逊的妻子，还没有完全放弃挽回他的希望。

sentences.en: So when he won the Battle of Copenhagen, she wrote him a letter of congratulation, which he completely and utterly ignored.
sentences.zh: 所以当他赢得哥本哈根战役时，她写了一封祝贺信给他，但他完全彻底地无视了。

sentences.en: And Edmund, his father, wrote to tell him off and said, Fanny, your wife was heavily affected with her personal feelings and not receiving a line from your own hand.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲埃德蒙写信责备他，说，范妮，你的妻子因为没收到你亲笔写的一行字而深受个人情感的折磨。

sentences.en: And Nelson said to his father, I don't care.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊对父亲说，我不在乎。

sentences.zh: 我的心意已决。

sentences.zh: 我想独处，不想让她过问。

sentences.en: Alexander Davison what I find a very, very sad and moving letter.

sentences.en: She said, when she heard Nelson was coming home, my heart was all thankfulness and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 然后我认为这是最悲伤的部分。

sentences.zh: 那是无意识的，没有任何意图。

sentences.zh: 但我希望，我的愿望是取悦他。

sentences.zh: 如果他能大发慈悲派人来接我，我会努力顺从他的每一个愿望。

sentences.zh: 她就是不明白她已经无能为力了。

sentences.zh: 而在纳尔逊的例子中，艾玛做到了。

sentences.en: He replies to all the demands that he see Fanny and says that he's committed to building his life around a wife more suited to my genius.
sentences.zh: 他回复了所有要求他见范妮的请求，并说他致力于围绕一个“更适合我天才”的妻子来建立自己的生活。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't think you could get away with saying that today.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我不认为你今天能逃脱这种说法。

sentences.en: Could you?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, people would think very poorly of you.
sentences.zh: 我是说，人们会觉得你很糟糕。

sentences.en: I think you can if you're Nelson.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你是纳尔逊，你就可以。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously it's terrible.
sentences.zh: 我是说，显然这很糟糕。

sentences.en: He treats Fanny terribly.
sentences.zh: 他对待范妮太糟糕了。

sentences.en: You know, we've gone through that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们已经讨论过这一点了。

sentences.en: At the same time, I guess you're with someone you find boring.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我想如果你和一个你觉得无聊的人在一起。

sentences.en: You meet someone you find intoxicating.
sentences.zh: 你遇到了一个让你觉得陶醉的人。

sentences.en: What are you going to do?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么做？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Do you know who agrees with you?
sentences.zh: 你知道谁同意你的观点吗？

sentences.en: Theo, because he's written in the chat, enough about Fanny.
sentences.zh: 西奥，因为他在聊天室里写道，关于范妮的讨论到此为止。

sentences.en: It's poor from Theo.
sentences.zh: 西奥的表现真差劲。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So since Theo is our overlord, we'll get to the end.
sentences.zh: 既然西奥是我们的“霸主”，那我们就结束吧。

sentences.en: On the 1st of July, Nelson arrives back in London and he goes straight to the Admiralty.
sentences.zh: 7月1日，纳尔逊回到伦敦，直接去了海军部。

sentences.en: Now, in the eyes of the Admiralty, he has redeemed himself.
sentences.zh: 现在，在海军部眼中，他已经完成了自我救赎。

sentences.en: He has upheld Britain's national security.
sentences.zh: 他维护了英国的国家安全。

sentences.en: He has reaffirmed the Royal Navy's command of the seas.
sentences.zh: 他重申了皇家海军对海洋的控制权。

sentences.en: And there's never any whisper, is there, of criticism for him about disobeying orders?
sentences.zh: 从来没有任何关于他违抗命令的批评声，不是吗？

sentences.en: No, just like Capes and Vincent.
sentences.zh: 没有，就像圣文森特角之战一样。

sentences.en: If you gamble and it pays off, you're laughing.
sentences.zh: 如果你赌赢了，你就是赢家。

sentences.en: And he's done it not just by killing, but by diplomacy.
sentences.zh: 他不仅通过杀戮，还通过外交手段做到了这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the really impressive thing about Nelson at Copenhagen.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是纳尔逊在哥本哈根战役中真正令人印象深刻的地方。

sentences.en: You know, he's proved himself a politician as well as a warrior.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他不仅证明了自己是一位战士，也证明了自己是一位政治家。

sentences.en: But when he gets to the Admiralty, long faces greet him.
sentences.zh: 但当他回到海军部时，迎接他的是一张张愁云惨淡的脸。

sentences.en: Because while he has been away, there has been bombshell intelligence from across the channel.
sentences.zh: 因为在他离开期间，海峡对岸传来了一个重磅情报。

sentences.en: Because while Nelson has been in the Baltic, the new first consul of France, Napoleon Bonaparte, has been raising an enormous new army.
sentences.zh: 因为在纳尔逊身处波罗的海时，法国新任第一执政拿破仑·波拿巴已经集结了一支庞大的新军队。

sentences.en: And this time, I am sorry to say, Bonaparte's target is not Naples or Constantinople or Egypt.
sentences.zh: 而这一次，很遗憾，波拿巴的目标不是那不勒斯、君士坦丁堡或埃及。

sentences.en: His cruel and greedy eyes are set on the coast of England.
sentences.zh: 他那贪婪而残忍的目光，正盯着英格兰的海岸。

sentences.en: And absolute scenes.
sentences.zh: 场面简直乱成一团。

sentences.en: So will Napoleon try an evasion of England?
sentences.zh: 那么，拿破仑会尝试入侵英格兰吗？

sentences.en: Will Nelson be able to stop him?
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊能阻止他吗？

sentences.en: There is literally only one way to find out.
sentences.zh: 答案只有一个。

sentences.en: And that is to listen to our next episode, which will be out on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 那就是收听我们的下一期节目，它将于周四发布。

sentences.en: If you are not a club member, but if you are a club member, you can hear that.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是会员，但如果你是会员，你现在就能听到。

sentences.en: And the final two episodes of this epic series straight away.
sentences.zh: 以及这个史诗系列最后两集的全部内容。

sentences.en: And if you are not a club member and you would like to be able to hear these episodes immediately, then you just have to go to therestishistory.com and sign up there.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是会员，但想立即收听这些节目，只需前往 therestishistory.com 注册即可。

sentences.en: And of course, it comes with a whole slew of additional benefits, doesn't it, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 当然，这还附带了一大堆额外福利，对吧，多米尼克？

sentences.en: One of which, this week, coming out on Friday, I will be talking to Mary Beard about another great military commander, Julius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是本周五发布的内容，我将与玛丽·比尔德探讨另一位伟大的军事统帅——尤利乌斯·凯撒。

sentences.en: So just sensational value, as we have said.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，这简直物超所值。

sentences.en: Wonderful stuff.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Dominic, thanks so much for that.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，非常感谢。

sentences.en: We will be back with Napoleon's greedy eyes set on England, and we will see you then.
sentences.zh: 我们将带着拿破仑那贪婪的目光重回英格兰，到时见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
